c0032: Card and mobile wallet (contactless) processing fees on total sales. Ask your POS provider for its rate
c0044: Security deposit, in months of rent. The example uses two; commercial leases commonly ask for one to three, and some landlords also want a personal guarantee: check it with your attorney
c0053: Owner's cash. Lenders usually expect an owner equity injection (often around 10% for SBA start-ups; many want 20-30%) toward the cash need
c0055: Principal requested. The "Financing" tab compares what you put in with the cash need on "Startup Costs" and tells you whether you have a surplus or a shortfall: adjust the loan with that figure. The example is an SBA 7(a) loan, which you apply for through your lender (SBA Microloans go up to $50,000)
c0063: Three months of fixed costs: the cushion for the ramp-up, which with Month 1 in January falls on the slowest months of the year (January and February)
c0102: Month of the 12-Month Cash Flow in which a summer extra payment falls. It only matters if you enter more than 12 pay periods; with 12 there are no extra payments. If you use it, July is Month 7, because Month 1 of the plan is January
c0104: Month of the 12-Month Cash Flow in which a holiday extra payment falls. It only matters if you enter more than 12 pay periods; with 12 there are no extra payments. If you use it, December is Month 12, because Month 1 of the plan is January
c0175: LLC formation (or an S corp election with your CPA), business license, local fees, health permit and the written food safety plan. Government fees carry no sales tax; professional fees may, depending on your state: change the column next to it if your quote is mostly professional fees
c0230: The monthly amount is on the "0. Assumptions" tab; here it is multiplied by twelve. The two months of rent before opening are on "Startup Costs" and are NOT counted twice
c0238: Bookkeeping, income tax and payroll filings for the LLC, payroll processing and the staff paperwork (offer letters, I-9, W-4)
c0250: Contract with a licensed pest control operator: it is part of the prerequisites of your written food safety plan.
c0252: ASCAP, BMI and SESAC are separate licenses; the fee depends on the square footage and the seating of your shop
c0285: Ceiling for rent on sales for a space with a Type I hood and exhaust to the roof: Kit estimate
c0317: Covers per day forecast in the plan
c0322: Covers per day needed to cover costs for each average check (columns) and each variable cost per cover (rows). Green cells are below the covers per day the plan forecasts.
c0323: Covers per day needed: average check excl. sales tax (columns) × variable cost per cover (rows)
c0336: Covers per day to break even
c0339: Covers per year per full-time equivalent
c0340: Covers each full-time employee in the "Staffing" tab would have to serve. In the optimistic scenario it tells you whether you need to hire
c0345: The "Base" column reads its three inputs from the "0. Assumptions" tab, so it reproduces EXACTLY year 1 of the P&L. The other two scenarios use the same cost rates: the only things that change are covers, average check and days. FIXED COSTS are the same in all three: miscellaneous and contingency, which is a percentage of sales, sits at the top with the variable costs and each scenario carries its own.
c0370: Coverage for vacations and the team's days off through the year. Paid sick leave is required by some states and cities: check yours
c0403: 1. "0. Assumptions" is the control sheet: covers per day, average check excl. sales tax, operating days, food and beverage mix, cost of goods sold, rent, financing and taxes.
c0405: 3. Only "Break-Even" is derived entirely from the rest. The other three tabs also have green cells you can edit: the pessimistic and optimistic scenarios in "Scenarios", seasonality and the launch ramp-up in "12-Month Cash Flow", and the other funding sources in "Financing" (rows 8-11 count as sources but are not amortized: Your bank or SBA 7(a) loan goes in "Loan requested" on "0. Assumptions"). Everything else is calculated.
c0409: 7. The "Financing" tab matches what you need with what you put in and builds the amortization schedule of the loan. If the difference is red, the plan is not funded.
c0421: Covers per day for the ACCOUNTING break-even (depreciation included)
c0539: Measures how long the business takes to pay back the investment with what it generates BEFORE paying the lender, on the SAME cash flow basis in all three years; whether you can make the loan payment is answered by the DSCR on the "Financing" tab. The Word business plan quotes this figure; if you change a green cell, this workbook rules
